text.p: CS Holding expects savings from its restructuring programming, announced in July, to be on the order of over 700 million Swiss francs per year, chairman Rainer Gut said in speech released ahead of a shareholder meeting.
"Once the reorganisation is completed at the end of 1998, we expect to make cost savings on the order of more than 700 million Swiss francs per year," Gut said in the text of the speech.
He also reiterated that against this savings, there would be a one-off restructuring cost of one billion francs for which the group will make a provision in the 1996 acounting year.
Gut reminded shareholders that the one billion franc provision was covered by hidden reserves on long-term holdings in non-core business activities.
"As already announced, we will be disposing of these holdings at an appropriate juncture in the near future," Gut said.
Swiss analysts have been speculating about when CS Holding will sell off its 44.9 percent stake in power and building controls group Elektrowatt and in what form the sale would take place.
But Gut made no references to the Elektrowatt stake in the text of his speech.
The extraordinary shareholding meeting was called for the sole purpose of changing the group's name from CS Holding to Credit Suisse Group as part of its broad restructuring plan.
